trials that produced only sporadic responses — and the exploratory analysis attributed that to
infrequent actual MET *activation*. Expression is not a target; measured activation is. ⛔ **RET in EMC
has NOT PASSED that test — it has not TAKEN it, and the sentence that stood here overstated the
record.** *Superseded, retained: "RET in EMC passes the test MET in CCS failed."* The CCS study is
specific about the instrument that decided MET: a **32-case blinded tissue microarray** staining
ligand, receptor, both activation-loop phospho-sites and three downstream nodes — MET protein in
**82 %** of cases and phospho-MET Tyr1234–35 in **4 %** (**PMID 34885165**, PMC8657105 **[FT]**).
**No equivalent measurement of RET exists in EMC**: the sole activation report is one sentence in
one paywalled abstract over *"a limited set of samples"* of an n = 10 series, with no numerator and
no denominator (**PMID 24703573**), and the same group had already recorded that they *"could not
assess the RTK activation profile"* for want of untreated frozen material (**PMID 23058004**,
PMC3534218 **[FT]**). One home for every sentence quoted here:
[`emc-ret-activation-bar.json`](../modalities/emc-ret-activation-bar.json).
map_edits_required.why: the memo's strongest sentence asserts that a test was passed; the sources show the test was never administered. Expression common + activation frequency unreported IS the MET failure shape, not its opposite

map_edits_required.anchor: **Free next step.** Test whether *RET* is a fusion target gene: an NBRE-motif scan of its regulatory
map_edits_required.current_text:
**Free next step.** Test whether *RET* is a fusion target gene: an NBRE-motif scan of its regulatory
region, the same bioinformatic approach that established *PPARG* and *ENO3* as direct targets, plus a
read across the public EMC expression series. **What would kill it:** no NBRE at *RET*, plus evidence
that RET phosphorylation tracks stromal rather than tumour content.
map_edits_required.proposed_text:
**Free next step.** ⚠ **RE-SPECIFIED 2026-08-07 — the step as written could not deliver what it
promised.** *Superseded, retained: "the same bioinformatic approach that established PPARG and ENO3
as direct targets".* The ENO3 source (**PMID 26310886**) used **EMSAs, ChIP assays and luciferase
reporters**, not a motif scan, and studied **TFG::NR4A3**, not the EMC-canonical EWSR1 fusion — so a
motif scan neither established ENO3 nor can establish RET. ⭐ The precedent that DID run this method
is already cited in [3.2](#32--fusion-variant-stratification) for a different purpose: **PMID
31020999** / PMC6766969 **[FT]** ran a MatInspector NBRE scan of SEMA regulatory regions and then
**confirmed the prediction by ChAP-qPCR** — finding that *EWSR1*-NR4A3 binds the SEMA3C element and
*TAF15*-NR4A3 does not, which is a mechanism-level bridge from this lane to §3.2's response split.
With no wet lab, a motif scan here yields a **prioritisation, never a target-gene claim**. The scan,
its two composition-matched nulls and the EMC expression read are **built and tested** in
[`emc_ret_target_scan.py`](../modalities/emc_ret_target_scan.py); the highest-value step is instead
asking whether **any NR4A3 / EWSR1::NR4A3 ChIP-seq cistrome exists at all**, which would answer the
question outright. **What would kill it:** unchanged — no NBRE at *RET*, **plus** evidence that RET
phosphorylation tracks stromal rather than tumour content. ⚠ **Neither clause has been measured**;
the artifact records both as `NOT_RUN`, not as negatives.

record.title: Selective RET inhibition in EMC
record.purpose: Is RET a real, activated, druggable effector in EMC — and if it is, can an agent approved for RET-altered disease reach a tumour whose RET is over-expressed wild type?

grade.value: Real but over-ranked on entry. The expression signal is genuine and reproduced in two independent cohorts; the ACTIVATION claim rests on one sentence over an unquantified subset of a ten-patient series, and the approved selective agents' evidence base is RET-ALTERED disease, which EMC is not. Neither clause of its stated falsifier has been measured.

record.rationale: Sunitinib produced 6 partial responses in 10 EMC patients, and among its putative targets only RET was reported as expressed and activated (PMID 24703573). An independent six-patient transcriptome cohort found RET the only sunitinib-target kinase significantly enriched in EMC versus other sarcomas (PMID 28423517). If the fusion drives RET transcriptionally, RET becomes a downstream node reachable without solving the paralogue-selectivity or ternary-geometry problems the driver-directed routes are blocked on.
remaining_unknowns: The FRACTION of EMC tumours with activated RET. The only report describes 'a limited set of samples' from an n=10 series with no numerator or denominator, and the full text is paywalled — this is the single unknown the whole route turns on.

Whether RET is a TARGET GENE of EWSR1::NR4A3 at all. No cistrome of the FUSION exists — only single-locus chromatin work at SEMA3C (PMID 31020999) and ENO3 (PMID 26310886, on TFG::NR4A3). Wild-type NR4A3 ChIP-seq DOES exist (PMID 36482877 human cDC2s, all three paralogues; PMID 42028030 Schwann cells, GSA CRA032324) and intersecting those peaks with RET is a $0 step that outranks the motif scan.
Whether a bulk RTK-activation read in a hypocellular, matrix-rich tumour reports tumour-cell or stromal signalling — the route's own falsifier, and untested.
Whether any selective RET inhibitor has activity against over-expressed wild-type RET. Every approval enrolled RET-fusion- or RET-mutation-positive disease; 2,077 records surfaced no counter-example.

required_validation.what: A phospho-RET tissue microarray across an EMC series, with ligand and downstream nodes, of the kind that decided MET in clear cell sarcoma (PMID 34885165)

Intersect the published wild-type NR4A3 ChIP-seq peak sets with the RET locus — measured occupancy in real chromatin rather than a sequence motif. Carries a paralogue-overlap read for free, since one dataset ChIP'd NR4A1, NR4A2 and NR4A3 in the same cells
An NBRE/NurRE scan of RET's regulatory region against composition-matched nulls, plus the EMC expression contrast — a prioritisation, explicitly not a binding claim
Confirmation that any predicted element is actually occupied by the chimera, by ChAP-qPCR or ChIP as in PMID 31020999

readiness.why_not_higher: The route's headline claim did not survive contact with its own sources, and the two measurements that would settle it are a paywalled page and a wet-lab assay. What IS publishable today is the negative-shaped finding — that the sole basis for calling RET activated in EMC is an unquantified subset of ten patients — and that belongs in the lane memo before it belongs in a route paper.
missing: the full text of Eur J Cancer 2014;50:1657-64 (PMID 24703573)
the RET regulatory-sequence and EMC-expression fetch, which needs one CI dispatch

timing.rationale: The cheapest decisive step is not compute and not money: it is one paywalled methods section. Until the activation denominator is known, any further investment risks building on a claim that a single unread page could remove.
timing.six_month_delta: Only if an NR4A3 cistrome or an EMC phospho-RET series is published.
timing.two_year_delta: An EMC model with public transcriptomes, or any tumour-agnostic trial admitting RET overexpression rather than RET alteration, would change the route materially.
timing.automation_outlook: The motif scan and the expression read are fully automated and cost $0. Nothing else about this route is.

record._why_those_retirements: a downstream-node route needs no NR4A3 binder, no ternary geometry and no paralogue discrimination — it inherits a different and arguably harder problem instead (is the node actually driving anything?), which is what `remaining_unknowns` records.

publication.contribution: The RET arm, and — more usefully in its current state — the negative that the only published basis for calling RET an activated target in EMC is an unquantified subset of a ten-patient series, which nobody has said out loud in twelve years.

distinct_from.axis: which target the TKI activity is attributed to
distinct_from.why: the existing sunitinib/pazopanib rows attribute EMC's TKI activity to antiangiogenesis and carry the clinical series; this route makes RET the claimed effector, which is a mechanistic claim the antiangiogenic reading does not need and which the originating authors themselves did not adopt

record.closure_note: Open. The decisive unknown is a denominator that exists in a paywalled methods section.
